content.value_statement: Large codebases hide repeated structures and inconsistent decisions. This skill maps design patterns, architecture, conventions, duplication, and anti-patterns with evidence and recommendations.
actual_capabilities: Identifies common creational, structural, and behavioral design patterns.
Maps architectural styles, layers, module boundaries, and data flow.
Finds recurring code structures, naming conventions, and file organization.
Highlights duplication and anti-patterns with referenced locations.
Provides prioritized refactoring and consistency recommendations.
Runs a bundled regex detector across supported source file extensions.
limitations: Pattern identification depends on available source files and representative examples.
The bundled detector uses signatures and can miss implicit or unusual implementations.
Architectural conclusions require human review when boundaries or runtime behavior are unclear.
Several resources and scripts named in the guide are not included in this package.

use_cases.title: Review an unfamiliar codebase
use_cases.description: Map dominant patterns, layers, conventions, and data flow before making changes.

use_cases.title: Plan focused refactoring
use_cases.description: Locate repeated structures and anti-patterns, then prioritize practical consolidation work.

use_cases.title: Document architecture decisions
use_cases.description: Create an evidence-based overview of patterns, boundaries, strengths, and inconsistencies.

prompt_templates.title: Identify design patterns
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze [directory] for design patterns. Name each pattern, cite its locations, and explain its purpose.
prompt_templates.scenario: Start with a focused pattern inventory.

prompt_templates.title: Find repeated code structures
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [directory] for repeated structures and conventions. Separate useful consistency from duplication that should be refactored.

prompt_templates.title: Assess application architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Map the architecture of [project]. Describe layers, module boundaries, data flow, dependencies, strengths, and structural concerns with evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Create a refactoring roadmap
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze [project] for patterns and anti-patterns. Rank improvements by impact, risk, effort, and affected locations.
prompt_templates.scenario: Turn pattern evidence into an advanced improvement plan.

output_examples.input: Analyze the service directory for design patterns.
output: Repository pattern: Three data access classes isolate persistence concerns.
Strategy pattern: Two pricing implementations share a stable selection interface.
Priority: Standardize repository error handling across all implementations.

output_examples.input: Find repeated validation logic in the application.
output: Three validation flows perform the same normalization and required-field checks.
The shared behavior is suitable for one reusable validator.

output_examples.output: The project uses layered architecture with presentation, service, and data access boundaries. Two presentation modules bypass the service layer and need review.

best_practices: Specify the directory, language, and analysis goal before starting.
Request file and line evidence for every reported pattern.
Validate recommendations against runtime constraints and team conventions.
anti_patterns: Do not infer architecture from directory names alone.
Do not treat every repeated structure as harmful duplication.
Do not recommend design patterns without a concrete maintenance benefit.

faq.question: Which patterns can this skill identify?
faq.answer: It covers common design, architecture, data, testing, module, asynchronous, and organization patterns.

faq.question: Does it modify source code?
faq.answer: No. The documented workflow reads and searches code, then reports findings and recommendations.

faq.question: Can it find duplicate code?
faq.answer: It can identify similar structures and likely duplication, but detailed similarity measurement may require additional tooling.

faq.question: Does it support every programming language?
faq.answer: The methodology is general, while the bundled detector supports TypeScript, JavaScript, Python, Java, Go, and Rust file extensions.

faq.question: How reliable are detected patterns?
faq.answer: Reliability improves when findings include implementation evidence, usage context, and multiple supporting locations.

faq.question: What should I provide for the best result?
faq.answer: Provide the target directory, important constraints, known architecture, and the decisions you need the analysis to support.
